subject: general
question: When a current twice its rated current flows through a fuse element, how much time does it take to melt?
solution:
__**Concept:**__

A fuse operates on the heating effect of current (I²t rule). When the current increases, the heating increases rapidly, causing the fuse element to melt faster.

For most standard fuse elements:

• At twice the rated current, the fuse typically blows in a short time (not instantly). • The melting time is governed by the I&am
